analysis.title: HSBC Destroys Goldman's CoreWeave Upgrade: "The More It Invests, The More The Value Destruction"; Sees Crash To $39
key_insights: HSBC (Abhishek Shukla) reiterated Reduce on CoreWeave with a $39 price target, 36.5% below Friday's close, one day after Goldman (Gabriela Borges) upgraded to Buy and cut its target from $139 to $106. The stock spiked to $66 on the upgrade, then gave back the entire gain.

HSBC estimates CoreWeave earns an average 2026-30e ROIC of 8.9% including customer advances and negative working capital, below its cost of borrowing. HSBC's view is that more investment at this return profile adds more value destruction.

HSBC uses the same 10% long-term pretax cost of debt as Goldman. Its WACC is 9.7%, below the 11.8% Goldman used in its illustrative contract math. The gap between $39 and $106 comes from revenue per MW, margins and interest costs.

HSBC expects CoreWeave revenue of $12 million per MW per year in 2027, versus $17-18 million for hyperscalers. It attributes the gap to hyperscalers' short-term contracts, differentiated general-purpose cloud business and many small customers that buy the full stack.

In HSBC's revenue-per-gigawatt math, CoreWeave earns about $12.1 billion per Nvidia-equivalent GW in 2027, versus $18.2 billion for Microsoft Azure and $21.7 billion for AWS. Only Oracle's cloud is comparable.

HSBC argues neoclouds have weak balance sheets and depend on debt, so lenders require long-term contracts with large creditworthy customers that cover the full repayment period. This keeps them out of the short-term rental market.
HSBC calculates CoreWeave's RPO covers 5.0 years of cloud revenue, versus 2.5 years at Amazon and 3.4 years at Google and Microsoft.

Revenue is about 33% of gross assets ex-construction and leases. With GPUs depreciated over six years, depreciation is roughly 50% of revenue. Data center rent is 17-18% and power 5-6%, so over 70% of costs are fixed. HSBC's long-term non-GAAP operating margin is 15-16%, versus management's guidance of about 25%.
HSBC has CoreWeave ROIC at 4.9% in 2027 and 5.0% in 2030 (high single digits including customer advances), versus AWS in the mid-to-high teens and Microsoft around 14%.

Goldman cited short-term (3-6 month) contracts signing at $40 million per MW, about 4x the blended portfolio. HSBC agrees those deals happened but expects them not to last, because LLM provider revenue growth has moderated over the last three months.
By the article's chart reading, LLM provider run-rate revenue rose from about $44 billion in March to about $105 billion in July, then to about $115 billion by September.
HSBC notes SpaceX's May deals with Anthropic and Google, which could earn SpaceX $22-50 million per MW, are cancellable on three months' notice.

Goldman's FICC desk (Mark Wilson) named two catalysts for last week's sharp price moves: CoreWeave co-founder McBee's comments on insurance capital availability, and a debate over frontier-lab business models and closed versus open model competition.

Goldman argued CoreWeave's 13.5-15% unsecured yields are not representative of its cost of debt because the unsecured market has been closed to new issuance. HSBC reads yields of 14-15% as market concern over creditworthiness that limits financing of speculative or short-contract capacity.

HSBC says consensus assumes a significant cut in CoreWeave's borrowing rate, which it considers increasingly unlikely. Its implied interest rate is 9.0% in 2029 versus 7.8% for the Street, a 112bps gap.
Five-year CDS closed at a record 1,117bps last Wednesday. The 2031 bonds yield just over 15%, off a 16%+ peak last week.
HSBC is 9.6% below consensus on 2030 revenue. Its 2030 non-GAAP operating profit of $11.2 billion is 46% below consensus, and its 2028-2030 EPS estimates are 54-71% below consensus.

Goldman raised its 2028 EPS to $3.36, 3.5x HSBC's $0.96. Goldman's base case has FCF turning positive in 2030, while HSBC has FCF at -$22.9 billion in 2027 and -$5.9 billion in 2030, with net debt rising from $17.5 billion at end-2025 to $92.3 billion by 2030.
HSBC expects CoreWeave to stay loss-making through 2029 if share-based compensation is treated as an expense.
CoreWeave trades at 14.7x 2030e EV/non-GAAP EBIT after SBC versus 7-11x for hyperscalers, and at 0.78x EV/RPO versus 0.34x for Oracle. HSBC calls the premium unsustainable.

Street targets range widely against a premarket price of about $58.6: HSBC $39 (33% downside), Goldman $106, BNP Paribas $117 (recently cut), Evercore ISI $150 and another at $169, implying 81% to 156% upside. JPMorgan said debt fears are overdone but expects negative FCF until 2030.

HSBC has held Reduce since initiating in July 2025 with a $32 target when the stock was around $120. Its target has ranged between $32 and $44. Goldman's disclosures show a pending CoreWeave underwriting, a 1%+ holding and banking fees, while HSBC's disclosure checklist is blank.
HSBC argues poor asset turnover reflects weak competitive dynamics, not short-term growth pains, so depreciation is unlikely to fall as a share of revenue.
Neocloud peers are weak. Korea's Elice fell as much as 32% on its debut, and Gartner predicted over 80% of neoclouds will fold by 2030. Meta earnings tomorrow are the next test of customer capex.

Goldman upgraded on the spread between unlevered IRR and WACC, a 10% cost of new debt and new contracts at about $13 million per MW. It cut its target from $139.
BNP Paribas recently cut its target to $117 from a higher level, per the article.
Evercore ISI target cited as part of the range of Street targets implying 81% to 156% upside.
JPMorgan said debt fears are overdone, though it still expects free cash flow to stay negative until 2030, per Investing.com.

tension_points.theme: CoreWeave returns and cost of capital
tension_points.bull_case: Goldman argues investors overestimate the rise in cost of capital and underestimate pricing per MW. It assumes new contracts at about $13 million per MW, pricing biased to the upside over 24 months, 3-6 month contracts at $40 million per MW, and FCF turning positive in 2030 to make CoreWeave self-funded.
tension_points.bear_case: HSBC argues ROIC of 8.9% is below the cost of borrowing, neocloud pricing is structurally capped by weak balance sheets and bare-metal customers, margins are held down by over 70% fixed costs, and the unsecured bond market (14-15% yields) is closed to speculative capacity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Goldman's bull case needs pricing per MW to rise by a third, the spot market to stay hot and financing to stay open on attractive terms. Moderating LLM revenue growth or a capex cut by CoreWeave's biggest customers (Meta earnings the next test) would undercut it.
